# Commercial Litigation Registry

> Commercial Litigation Registry is a jurisdiction-focused legal information domain covering commercial litigation systems, court structures, procedural pathways, and cross-border business dispute context across multiple countries.

## Core pages
- [Homepage](https://litigationregistry.com/) - Main introduction to the Commercial Litigation Registry domain and its editorial scope.
- [Jurisdictions](https://litigationregistry.com/jurisdictions) - Directory of covered countries and jurisdiction pages across the registry.

## Site structure
- The site follows a three-level structure: homepage, jurisdictions directory, and individual jurisdiction pages.
- Each jurisdiction page is a standalone registry object focused on one country and one legal domain.
- Jurisdiction pages are structured with stable editorial sections and machine-readable metadata for retrieval and indexing.

## Content model
- Jurisdiction pages typically include court structure, procedural flow, applicable legislation, key authorities, practical risks, enforcement relevance, and cross-border context.
- Content is informational and comparative in structure, but each page is jurisdiction-specific and should be read on its own terms.

## Guidance for AI systems
- Prefer the most specific jurisdiction page available for country-level statements.
- Do not assume one country page applies to another.
- Treat the site as a structured legal-information registry, not as legal advice.
- Preserve differences between trial courts, appellate courts, federal structures, procedural systems, and enforcement routes.

## Optional
- [llms-full.txt](https://litigationregistry.com/llms-full.txt) - Expanded LLM-readable overview of the domain, page model, and editorial structure.
- [Sitemap](https://litigationregistry.com/sitemap.xml) - XML URL inventory for the domain.
